statement.p: Let f(x) = \ln{(x)}. Solve each of the following equations exactly for x.

static.solution:
SOLUTION
(a) Since \left( f(x) \right)^{-1} = \frac{1}{f(x)} = \frac{1}{\ln{(x)}}, this equation is equivalent to \frac{1}{\ln{(x)}} = 16 or \ln{(x)} = \frac{1}{16}. Taking the exponential of both sides, we obtain x = e^{1/16}, so the solution is x = e^{1/16}.
(b) Since the inverse function of \ln{(x)} is given by f^{-1}(x) = e^x, this equation is equivalent to e^x = 16. Taking the natural logarithm of both sides, we obtain a solution of x = \ln{(16)}.
(c) This equation is equivalent to \ln{(1/x)} = 16. Taking the exponential of both sides, we obtain \frac{1}{x} = e^{16}, so the final answer is given by x = e^{-16}.
